newsitem.title: USA: Repairs hold up N.J. Salem 2 nuke restart approval.
newsitem.headline: Repairs hold up N.J. Salem 2 nuke restart approval.

text.p: Last minute repairs are holding up Nuclear Regulatory Commission's (NRC) approval to restart the 1,106 megawatt (MW) Salem 2 nuclear power unit in southern New Jersey, an NRC spokesman said Friday.
"The hold-up is on the plant's end...The plant is trying to fix some leaking valve," said the spokesman, referring to the current work on the unit's spray valve.
Salem 2 cooled to "hot shutdown" from "hot standby" status midweek to correct the spray valve problem.
The operator, Public Service Electric & Gas Co (PSE&G), had planned to ramp up the unit to service by the end of July pending approval from the NRC.
Salem 2 and the adjoining unit Salem 1, with the same generating capacity, have been shut for more than two years due to safety concerns raised by the commission.
"The plant has adequately addressed all the safety issues. We're waiting to hear from them about those last minute problems," the NRC spokesman said.
Salem 1 is tentatively scheduled to resume operation late this year.
PSE&G was not immediately available for comment.
In addition to PSE&G, PECO Energy Co, Atlantic Energy Co and Delmarva Power & Light Co are the other owners of the Salem units.
